full_judgment:
9. There is no dispute regarding the fact aforesaid. The learned Counsel for the respondents submitted that the disputed land was khas land of the Maliks which were held directly under the Government and used as residential house with building thereon from long before the coming into force of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. The provisions of Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act does not therefore, apply to the suit property as it was not non-agricultural land held by a non-agricultural tenant. This was not controverted by the appellants. 

 10. In view of the fact established by the affidavit referred to above, the statements made therein, and documents annexed thereto, it appears that the land in dispute was Nishkar khas land of the Maliks held directly under the Government and used as residential house with building long before the coming into force of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. It, therefore, follows that Section 23 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is not attracted in the present case. In view of our decision there is no necessity to consider whether the Muslim law would prevail over the aforesaid Act.
